summary: This informational document defines Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) attributes that bring functions common in 3G and 4G networks, such as Access Point Name selection, to Wi-Fi access networks that connect to the mobile Evolved Packet Core.

plainLanguage.summary: Phone companies use Wi-Fi too. This note adds labels to the login process so Wi-Fi can offer things their cell networks already do.

subtitle: Six new EAP-AKA attributes let a phone ask a trusted Wi-Fi network for the same services its cellular network offers.

tldr.problem: Mobile operators want Wi-Fi to offer functions common in 3G and 4G, such as choosing an Access Point Name (APN), holding several packet data connections, and moving a session between Wi-Fi and cellular.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines six new skippable EAP-AKA attributes that a Mobile Node and the operator's AAA server exchange during EAP authentication, and that act as triggers for Proxy Mobile IPv6 nodes.
tldr.outcome: The attributes were assigned numbers 145 to 150 in the IANA registry. The document is Informational, not a standard, and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 7458 is an Informational document. It has not been obsoleted or updated according to the RFC metadata, and it defines the EAP attribute numbers 145 to 150.

sections.title: Why Wi-Fi Needs Cellular Functions
sections.content:
Wi-Fi has become a trusted access technology for mobile service providers. Work such as IEEE 802.11u and HotSpot 2.0 lets a Mobile Node (MN) pick a Wi-Fi network much as it would roam onto a cellular one, so functions that 3G and 4G networks provide are wanted in Wi-Fi too.

This RFC defines new EAP attributes for three functions: APN selection, multiple APN connectivity, and mobility between Wi-Fi and UTRAN/E-UTRAN (3G/4G radio access). They work with EAP-AKA (RFC 4187) and EAP-AKA' (RFC 5448). Because they share one IANA registry, they also apply to EAP-SIM.

The attributes also act as a trigger for Proxy Mobile IPv6 nodes. For example, when the MN asks for a new IP session and the network agrees, the attribute lets the Mobile Anchor Gateway (MAG) start a new mobility session with the Local Mobility Anchor (LMA).
sections.plainLanguage: Phone companies already let your phone pick services and switch between networks. This RFC teaches Wi-Fi to do the same by adding a few extra notes to the login message.

sections.title: How EAP Runs Over Wi-Fi
sections.content:
In a Wi-Fi network, EAP is carried over IEEE 802.1X, which is a transparent mechanism that does not look inside the authentication messages. The endpoints of the EAP method are the MN and the AAA server; the Wi-Fi Access Node (WAN) in between simply relays.

The RFC's example flow runs: beacon and probe, 802.11 authentication and association, then EAP Request/Identity, the MN's EAP Response/Identity, an EAP Request/AKA-Challenge, an EAP Response/AKA-Challenge, and finally EAP Success. After that an end-to-end data path exists and the MN can start DHCPv4 or IPv6 Router Solicitation.

The document uses the full EAP Authentication procedure. Use of EAP Fast Re-Authentication is left for further study.
sections.plainLanguage: Your phone shows its ID, the network sends a secret question, the phone answers it, and then the door opens. The Wi-Fi box in the middle just passes the notes along.

sections.title: What the New Attributes Are For
sections.content:
Four jobs are covered. For APN selection, the MN includes AT_VIRTUAL_NETWORK_ID in its EAP-Response/AKA-Challenge to name the APN for its first connection. If it leaves the attribute out, the network may pick an APN by other means, which this RFC does not cover.

For connectivity type, the MN uses AT_CONNECTIVITY_TYPE to say whether it wants connectivity to the Evolved Packet Core or Internet offload (Non-Seamless Wireless Offload). The network replies with the same attribute in the EAP Success message.

For mobility, AT_HANDOVER_INDICATION says the MN wants to continue an IP session from UTRAN/E-UTRAN, and AT_HANDOVER_SESSION_ID may identify that earlier session. Finally, the MN serial ID carries the device's IMEI or IMEISV so the network can check that a legitimate, not stolen, device is in use. The AAA server MUST NOT pass it on to any other node.
sections.plainLanguage: The new boxes on the form say which service you want, whether you want the full phone network or just the Internet, whether you are carrying on a call from the cell network, and which device you are.

sections.title: The Attribute Formats
sections.content:
All the attributes follow the format of RFC 4187, and the Length field counts the first two bytes too. Each has a one-byte attribute number, a Length, and its own fields.

  • AT_VIRTUAL_NETWORK_ID carries an arbitrary octet string naming a virtual network, such as an APN in 3GPP E-UTRAN. It SHOULD be in the EAP-Response/AKA-Challenge.
  • AT_VIRTUAL_NETWORK_REQ has a Type (1 single PDN connection, 2 multiple PDN connections) and a Sub type (1 IPv4, 2 IPv6, 3 IPv4v6). From the MN it can appear only in EAP-Response/Identity; the network SHOULD include it in the EAP Request/AKA-Challenge.
  • AT_CONNECTIVITY_TYPE is 1 for Non-Seamless WLAN Offload or 2 for EPC PDN connectivity, and applies to multiple PDN connections only.
  • AT_HANDOVER_INDICATION is 0 for an independent new session, or 1 to hand over an existing one.
  • AT_HANDOVER_SESSION_ID has an Access Technology (1 UTRAN, 2 E-UTRAN) and a Session Id: the GUTI for E-UTRAN, or a 6-byte Global RNC ID followed by a 4-byte P-TMSI for UTRAN.
  • AT_MN_SERIAL_ID has a Serial ID Type (1 IMEI, 2 IMEISV). A network that needs it sends the attribute with no value, and the MN SHOULD answer inside AT_ENCR_DATA.
sections.plainLanguage: Each new box has a name tag and a few small answers to tick, like 1 for one choice and 2 for another. Together they make a tidy little card inside the login message.

sections.title: Security and Registry Entries
sections.content:
The attributes travel between the MN and the AAA server inside provider-controlled, trusted Wi-Fi networks, and the RFC argues that handling them is no worse than in existing 3G and 4G networks. They inherit the integrity, replay and confidentiality protection of the AKA or SIM method. AT_CONNECTIVITY_TYPE and AT_VIRTUAL_NETWORK_REQ must be integrity-protected with AT_CHECKCODE, as RFC 4187 requires. AT_MN_SERIAL_ID MUST have confidentiality protection, and an MN MUST NOT send it unless the request came from a network authenticated via EAP/AKA.

The RFC warns that identifiers like the IMEI could let devices be profiled and tracked. For IANA, the six attributes are numbered 145 to 150, and a new registry, Trusted Non-3GPP Access EAP Parameters, holds the Type and Sub type values (range 0 to 127, with 0 reserved) under the Specification Required policy.
sections.plainLanguage: The device number is private, like your home address, so it is locked in an envelope while it travels. Only the phone company opens it, and it must not hand it around.

items.label: AT_VIRTUAL_NETWORK_ID
items.desc: Names the virtual network (APN) to attach to.

items.label: AT_VIRTUAL_NETWORK_REQ
items.desc: Single or multiple PDN, plus IP version.

items.label: AT_HANDOVER_INDICATION
items.desc: Whether to hand over an existing IP session.

items.label: AT_MN_SERIAL_ID
items.desc: Device serial number such as IMEI or IMEISV.
